title: Colleague has a plan mode: hand it a vague or oversized assignment and it works backwards into a reviewed spec, turns that spec into a split plan, then runs the small items as a workforce of subagent colleagues — staged in small steps, not one big leap

claims.text: Colleague has a plan mode: hand it a vague or oversized assignment and it works backwards into a reviewed spec, turns that spec into a split plan, then runs the small items as a workforce of subagent colleagues — staged in small steps, not one big leap

honesty_conditions.text: With devague installed, 'colleague plan "<vague task>"' drives the staged arc to a reviewed spec, then a plan, then a workforce fan-out, pausing at every operator gate; with devague absent it fails fast with a precondition message, never a crash or a silent skip

'colleague plan "<vague task>"' runs the staged arc to a reviewed spec, then a plan, then a workforce fan-out, pausing at every operator gate, with NOTHING extra installed (native-first, zero deps); any devague fallback degrades gracefully when devague is absent, never crashing or silently skipping

claims.text: Operators — and delegating agents via ask-colleague — who hand colleague an assignment too vague or too large for a single bounded work item

honesty_conditions.text: A real class of assignments is genuinely too vague or too large for a single bounded colleague work item (today they hit auto-split or degradation); plan mode targets exactly those, not ordinary scoped tasks

claims.text: Colleague stages the assignment itself: idea -> reviewed spec (handled per-item), spec -> plan, plan -> small items, items -> a subagent-colleague workforce — each stage a discrete checkpoint, all inside the bounded loop

honesty_conditions.text: A single 'colleague plan' invocation carries an assignment through all four stages with checkpoints — the operator never hand-stitches think/spec-to-plan/assign-to-workforce for colleague's own planning

claims.text: Today colleague meets a too-big/too-vague task with a one-shot auto-split or graceful degradation; the staged spec->plan->workforce pipeline only exists as external Claude Code skills (think / spec-to-plan / assign-to-workforce) the operator drives by hand — colleague can't run it itself

honesty_conditions.text: Today colleague has no native staged planner — verifiable by the absence of a 'plan' verb in the CLI; the staged arc exists only as the Claude Code skills

claims.text: A vague or oversized assignment gets the same backwards-spec discipline — converge on evidence, not vibes — natively, repeatably and verifiably, instead of one lossy leap

honesty_conditions.text: A plan-mode spec exports only after its convergence gate passes (the same evidence discipline), so the output is a pressure-tested spec, not a one-shot guess — demonstrable by the gate refusing to export an unconverged frame

claims.text: A vague/oversized assignment yields a reviewed spec artifact, a split plan, and a workforce run, staged with checkpoints; fires identically for mock and vllm-openai; zero new runtime deps; strict no-op shape when plan mode isn't engaged

honesty_conditions.text: On a sample vague/oversized assignment, plan mode yields a reviewed spec + a split plan + a workforce run, identical in shape for mock and vllm-openai, with no new runtime dep and a byte-identical no-op when not engaged — checkable by the e2e shape test + zero-deps guard

claims.text: Not a daemon/server, not a multi-backend router, not auto-confirmation of its own spec (the spec-review checkpoint stays operator-owned, matching devague's user-only-confirm rule), not a reimplementation of subagents (reuses the existing fan-out/merge machinery), not a hard dependency on devague (degrades when absent)
Surface: a new agent-first verb 'colleague plan' with staged sub-states (plan status / plan continue), not a session toggle or a single loop tool

Gate model: between stages colleague stops at a file-based checkpoint (precedent: the flight control plane) and resumes via 'colleague plan continue'; the spec-review checkpoint is an operator gate, downstream stages may run autonomously once the spec is approved

Engine: the staged planner is native and zero-deps (colleague-owned plan artifact), optionally enriched by the existing devague loop tool when installed, degrading gracefully when absent (like the /tokenize carve-out)
The spec stage handles each spec item separately — a per-claim capture -> interrogate -> review micro-cycle — rather than capturing the whole spec in one turn

honesty_conditions.text: The spec stage surfaces one proposed item at a time and blocks on the operator's confirm/reject before proposing the next — demonstrable in a transcript of per-item gates, not a single bulk capture

claims.text: The workforce stage maps the plan's small items onto the existing subagents fan-out (dependency-aware waves), reusing make_batch_spawn / batch_spawn with no new worktree/merge code

Not a daemon/server, not a multi-backend router, not autonomous (every stage AND every sub-step is an operator gate; colleague never self-confirms a spec), not a reimplementation of subagents (the workforce reuses the existing fan-out/merge machinery), and not a reimplementation of devague/spec-to-plan (it orchestrates those CLIs)

Gate model: every stage AND every sub-step inside a stage is an operator gate (the announcement, each captured claim, each risk, each plan item, the workforce go/no-go). Colleague proposes via devague capture/interrogate; the operator runs confirm/reject. Nothing past a gate runs autonomously — plan mode is a guided, heavily-checkpointed flow, not fire-and-forget

Engine: plan mode orchestrates the real devague CLIs — 'devague' (idea->spec) and 'devague plan' (spec->plan) — driving their deterministic moves, and performs the workforce fan-out from 'devague plan waves' using colleague's own subagents machinery. 'colleague plan' therefore REQUIRES devague installed: a hard precondition for this verb (fails fast with a clear message when absent), unlike the rest of colleague where the devague tool is optional
The plan stage produces items each sized for one bounded child work item — granular in the plan stage as well as the spec stage — each carrying acceptance criteria and an honest dependency order

honesty_conditions.text: Each plan item carries acceptance criteria and is small enough that one child work item completes it within the step/token budget; the dependency order is explicit (waves), not implied

claims.text: Each gate is a durable file-based checkpoint (precedent: the flight control plane plus devague's own .devague state): 'colleague plan' stops with the proposed item + the recommended operator move surfaced, and 'colleague plan continue' resumes after the operator resolves it. No daemon, no socket

honesty_conditions.text: Killing colleague between stages or sub-steps and re-running 'colleague plan continue' resumes from the last resolved gate (state is entirely on disk); no daemon/socket/background process is required

claims.text: The workforce stage fans the plan's dependency waves out to parallel subagent colleagues in isolated worktrees with a sequential merge child, reusing make_batch_spawn / batch_spawn unchanged (caps unchanged: FANOUT=4, DEPTH=2) — TDD-gated merges, surfacing not force-merging conflicts

honesty_conditions.text: The fan-out calls colleague/subagents.py make_batch_spawn/batch_spawn unchanged (no new worktree/merge code), honours FANOUT=4/DEPTH=2, and surfaces unresolvable merge conflicts rather than force-merging

claims.text: devague is a subprocess CLI dependency for the 'colleague plan' verb, not a Python runtime dependency — 'dependencies = []' still holds (colleague shells out, same model as the existing culture/devague loop tools); only this one verb hard-requires the external CLI

honesty_conditions.text: The zero-deps guard still passes: 'colleague plan' invokes devague only via subprocess, never imports it; 'dependencies = []' is unchanged

claims.text: This is a deliberate re-spec expanding colleague's v1 scope with a new orchestration verb; it holds the conventions — zero Python runtime deps (devague is a subprocess precondition), no socket, no daemon (gates are file-based + resume), all-engines (orchestration/checkpoints/fan-out are runtime-owned; only proposal quality varies by backend)

Plan-mode steps carry a mandatory/optional attribute. Mandatory steps cannot be skipped and must be resolved at their gate — the announcement plus the devague convergence-required kinds (audience, after_state, before_state-or-why_it_matters, boundary, success_signal, and a confirmed honesty condition on every spec-affecting claim). Optional steps (extra risks, extra assumptions, nice-to-have claims) the operator may skip, and the skip is recorded

honesty_conditions.text: Proceeding past a mandatory step without resolving it is blocked (plan mode reuses the existing convergence gate's required-kinds rule rather than re-implementing it); skipping an optional step is permitted and recorded in the artifact

claims.text: Selected steps get an agent-reviewer critique pass BEFORE the operator gate: colleague runs the SAME backend model with a critic system prompt (an adversarial persona) over the proposed item and surfaces weaknesses, risks, and missing honesty conditions as advisory input. The reviewer never confirms — confirmation stays user-only. This intra-model critique (persona swap) is deliberately distinct from the different-backend diversity of ask-colleague / subagents

honesty_conditions.text: The reviewer is a second completion against config.model with a critic system prompt (no second model required); its critique is surfaced at the gate as non-authoritative input; with the reviewer disabled the propose->operator-gate flow is byte-identical, and it fires identically for mock and vllm-openai (all-engines)

claims.text: The agent-reviewer is same-model / different-system-prompt by default, on for consequential steps (the spec as a whole, each parked risk, the plan, the workforce go/no-go) and configurable/disableable; the critic prompt is a built-in plan-mode default, overridable via the existing layered AGENTS/skills config

Mandatory steps cannot be skipped and must be resolved at their gate: announcement, audience, after_state, before_state-or-why_it_matters, boundary, success_signal, and a confirmed honesty condition on every spec-affecting claim. Every other step (extra risks, extra assumptions, nice-to-have claims) is optional; the operator may skip it and the skip is recorded

honesty_conditions.text: Proceeding past a mandatory step without resolving it is blocked by plan mode's own native convergence check (the same required-kinds rule); skipping an optional step is permitted and recorded in the artifact

claims.text: Engine: plan mode drives the staged arc NATIVELY — a colleague-owned plan artifact plus its own staged capture/interrogate/converge/waves logic mirroring devague's methodology — so the verb carries NO hard dependency and 'dependencies = []' holds; it runs with nothing extra installed. devague is added as an optional subprocess fallback ONLY IF reimplementing its convergence/spec-to-plan/waves engine proves too costly. Native-first, devague-only-if-we-have-to

Not a daemon/server, not a multi-backend router, not autonomous (every stage AND every sub-step is an operator gate; colleague never self-confirms), not a reimplementation of subagents (the workforce reuses the existing fan-out/merge machinery). It DOES reimplement devague's planning methodology natively (native-first) rather than hard-depending on the devague CLI

honesty_conditions.text: Plan mode opens no socket and forks no daemon, never auto-confirms its own spec, and reuses colleague/subagents.py for the fan-out — verifiable by the boundary tests and the absence of a self-confirm path in colleague's own gate

claims.text: Plan mode keeps 'dependencies = []': the native arc imports no third-party package and shells out to nothing by default. Any future devague fallback is a subprocess CLI (never a Python import), so the zero-deps guard passes either way

honesty_conditions.text: The zero-deps guard still passes: plan mode imports no third-party package; any devague use is via subprocess only, never an import

claims.text: Overlap resolved: SAME arc, DIFFERENT planner. 'colleague plan' / 'ask-colleague plan' = COLLEAGUE is the planning mind; the 'think' skill = Claude is the planning mind. Parallel-by-design (the diversity is the point), not duplication

'ask-colleague' gains a 'plan' verb so a delegating agent (e.g. Claude) can hand the WHOLE planning arc to colleague — colleague does the planning — the inverse-skill surface mirroring how 'think' keeps Claude as planner

Deliberate re-spec expanding colleague's v1 scope with a new orchestration verb, holding the conventions: zero Python runtime deps (native-first; devague only as an optional subprocess fallback), no socket, no daemon (gates are file-based + resume), all-engines (orchestration/checkpoints/critique/fan-out are runtime-owned; only proposal quality varies by backend)

Colleague proposes via its native staged capture/interrogate; the operator confirms or rejects each one. Nothing past a gate runs autonomously — a guided, heavily-checkpointed flow, not fire-and-forget

Operators — and delegating agents via ask-colleague — who need colleague to handle genuinely COMPLEX implementations using the devague paradigm (spec -> plan -> workforce), not just single scoped work items

honesty_conditions.text: There is a real class of complex implementations colleague today cannot do well in one bounded work item; plan mode lets colleague carry them via the devague paradigm — verifiable on a sample complex task

claims.text: Plan mode has two entry paths: (1) explicit — invoked with 'colleague plan' / 'ask-colleague plan'; (2) automatic — during a normal work item colleague detects a feature that needs investigation (no clean implementation path) and triggers/suggests the spec-based devague-paradigm flow. Either path stages the assignment idea -> reviewed spec -> plan -> small items -> subagent-colleague workforce, each step a gated checkpoint

honesty_conditions.text: Both entry paths reach the SAME staged gated arc: 'colleague plan <task>' enters it explicitly, and a normal work item on a no-clean-path feature surfaces an advisory trigger into it

claims.text: Two reasons: colleague can carry genuinely complex tasks instead of degrading on them; and a DIFFERENT mind does the planning (the diversity is the value) — converging on evidence, not vibes

honesty_conditions.text: The planning mind is colleague (a different backend than the requesting agent) and the staged arc converges on confirmed evidence before any implementation

claims.text: Colleague can spec, plan, and implement a complex task end-to-end via the subagent-colleague workforce; AND it exercises judgment about WHEN to plan — pushing back when a task is too small for the pipeline, suggesting the spec-based flow when a task is hard. Fires identically for mock and vllm-openai; zero new runtime deps; strict no-op when not engaged

honesty_conditions.text: On a complex task colleague produces spec+plan+workforce implementation; on a trivially small task 'colleague plan' pushes back to a plain work item; on a hard normal task colleague suggests plan mode — all three observable, identical in shape for mock and vllm-openai, zero new deps

claims.text: Auto-trigger: beyond the explicit verb, during a normal work item colleague detects when a feature needs investigation (no clean implementation path / genuinely hard) and injects ONE advisory recommendation to enter the spec-based plan flow — precedent: the auto-split and capacity-warning recommendations; backend-judged, never a forced gate, strict no-op on a clear task

honesty_conditions.text: On a no-clean-path task colleague injects exactly ONE advisory plan-mode recommendation (like the auto-split recommendation); the model decides whether to act; on a clear scoped task it is a byte-identical no-op

claims.text: Pushback: colleague declines to spin up the full spec -> plan -> workforce pipeline for a clearly small/scoped task — it pushes back and recommends a direct 'colleague work' instead, rather than over-engineering a trivial task

honesty_conditions.text: Invoking 'colleague plan' on a trivially small task yields a pushback recommending a plain 'colleague work', not a full pipeline run
